text:
mei: quick report: new Next.js + LangChain starter in samples is causing confusing auth/retry behavior for newcomers. they copy the starter, leave the demo env var NEXT_PUBLIC_REDWOOD_KEY, and later complain about doubled token usage.

mei: repro steps I used:
1) clone github.com/redwood/samples/next-rag-quickstart
2) yarn && vercel dev
3) open app, ask a question, wait 20s, ask again -> Console shows 2 embed_calls for the single user-visible request.

darren: do you have the handler snippet? that pattern usually means the client and server are each calling the model, or there are hidden revalidation calls.

mei: handler is in /pages/api/query.js and the client fetches /api/query. but the starter's quick auth helper also runs a background refresh when the page becomes visible and it was configured to call a warmup endpoint that triggers an embed. oops.

lena: two separate DX issues: 1) the template exposes NEXT_PUBLIC env which teaches bad habits; 2) warmup middleware triggers model calls silently. proposed fixes: change examples to use server-only env names, remove warmup model call, and add a dev-only banner that shows "tokens last request: N" to help catch surprises.

darren: also suggest adding a small test in the starter's CI that runs the sample in headless mode and asserts Console telemetry delta <=1 per visible query. catches accidental background calls.

ci-bot: created issue #1988 in samples repo "next-rag-quickstart: avoid exposing keys in public env & remove hidden warmup calls" and linked PR template patch.

mei: i can open a PR to update the README and swap the env names, plus remove warmup. will include a note in the onboarding doc about "hidden calls increase billing".

lena: thanks mei. small follow-up: add a lint rule to samples to warn on NEXT_PUBLIC usage in starter code. That would prevent this class of error.

mei: will add lint in PR. pinging when ready. :thumbsup:
